utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning. We convene this morning for a Status Conference in the matter of the Prosecutor against Ivan Cermak and Mladen Markac. Mr. Scott?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Good morning, Ken Scott representing the Prosecution this morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Prodanovic.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. PRODANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour, on behalf of the accused Ivan Cermak, Cedo Prodanovic, and Ms. Jadranka Slokovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning. Mr. Separovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPAROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honour. On behalf of the accused Mladen Markac, my colleague Mr. Mikulicic, and myself, Miroslav Separovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. As the parties are aware the two accused are on release pending trial and for that reason are not present. Now, the reason, of course, for the Status Conference is that there must be one every 120 days, and that ensures that we continue to organise exchanges between the parties and the preparation for trial. The last one occurred early in February, so by virtue of time, it is necessary to hold this further conference at this stage. I notice that there are two pending motions. The first is an application by Ivan Cermak to amend the conditions of release, and there is a motion by the Prosecution to amend the indictment. I can tell you that each of those decisions are to be filed very shortly. Disclosure under Rule 66(A)(i) was completed last October. I assume it remains completed, and we must now check progress in respect of Rule 66(A)(ii) disclosure. I think it was mentioned when we were together in February by Mr. Scott that the Prosecution had disclosed 13 witness statements, but they were disclosed in English and the position about translations was not then resolved. The question arises whether those 13 statements have now been received by the Defence in B/C/S. Are you able to assist me there, Mr. Prodanovic and Mr. Separovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPAROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we have received this, but these have not been translated into Croatian.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That's the position also with you, is it, Mr. Prodanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PRODANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Precisely the same position.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Scott?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honour. May it please the Court, my understanding is that to respond to Your Honour generally as to the 68 disclosure, you're absolutely right, there has been very substantial Rule 68 disclosure in the past and as the Chamber knows, as Your Honour knows, that is a matter of ongoing disclosure as material is identified. As to the 66(A)(ii) material, I have to say that I'm not specifically in a position to either confirm or deny what the Defence has represented on these 13 items. I find that to be a bit surprising if that's the case but I'm not saying they are not right. I have to say, Your Honour, in terms of the material that I have in front of me this morning, in terms of some summary information that's been prepared for me, I don't think I have an answer to that specific question and our -- with my -- with my regret the regular case manager assigned to the case is not -- is not with us, is on leave at the moment, so I have a set of statistics here in front of me, Your Honour, but I don't see off-hand that it addresses -- that I can tell it addresses those specific 13 items. I can tell the Chamber that there has been substantial ongoing efforts to deal with translations and I think translations are being provided kind of on an as we go or rolling basis; by that, as they come in, they are disclosed. But I'm afraid at the moment, Your Honour, that's the best information I can give to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: That's about where we were on the 4th of February, Mr. Scott.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I understand Your Honour, and I regret that. All I can do is make further inquiries when I return to my office.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think an injection of some action as well might be useful as well as inquiries.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Beyond that you've moved and started to cover my next inquiry. That is whether there should be further statements beyond the 13 because whether we were last together it was indicated that you were continuing to approach other witnesses or potential witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour. There have been a small number. I think those documents -- again, those transcripts are in the process of being prepared. I think all of those or the vast majority of those have been recorded interviews. Just so the Court is not misled I think we are talking about a relatively small number. We are talking probably something in the vicinity of ten people or less. I don't want the Chamber to have the impression that we are talking about hundreds of additional statements. It's a small number. Again, Your Honour, there is a substantial -- unfortunately a substantial backlog of transcriptions in the OTP not only in this case but unfortunately in a number of cases and I cannot -- I cannot tell exactly which ones have been done at this particular moment. If the Defence has not received -- they are telling us they have not received any since the February Status Conference, I can certainly make further inquiries, again, and take some additional action when returning to my office.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think, Mr. Scott, it should be indicated that when we next meet, just short of another 120 days, I hope to hear from you not only the 13 but all witness statements have been provided, not only in English but also in the language of the accused. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I understand that, Your Honour. As I say the resources are being committed. Unfortunately it's not a problem unique to this case but I do expect very, very substantial progress will be made in the near future.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It affects the whole preparation for trial, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And there is a tendency in this case for it just to drift along.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Understood, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Defence counsel will have heard that in the view of the Chamber, it will be necessary for the Prosecution to provide you with all Rule 66(A)(ii) statements by the time of the next Status Conference, and to do so in both relevant languages. As Mr. Scott has indicated, the Prosecution are well aware that the Rule 68 disclosure obligation is ongoing. When we were last together Defence were having a technical problem with the electronic disclosure system. Has that now been overcome?

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPAROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I think we can put it that way. The problem has been overcome. We obtained some additional equipment and we now have access to all these documents. However, I do have to mention one thing. It's not really a major problem but I have to share this with my colleague, Mr. Scott. There are certain documents that keep reappearing in several different places in the files. There are documents that have not been located within the file and there is a special letter that we've written for the Prosecution in regard to this. There are some documents that get interrupted as we are using them. I can't say this presents a particular hindrance to the work of the Defence team but these are at any rate technical issues that we shall be clarifying with the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Separovic. Is there anything that you need to add to that, Mr. Prodanovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PRODANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour. We are facing the same sort of problem and we are dealing with them together. We also hope that we shall be able to resolve the matter in cooperation with the OTP. As my colleague Mr. Separovic said this is not a serious problem for the Defence at this stage and we hope to successfully resolve this matter over the following days.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes. Rule 70 disclosure, Mr. Scott? This was to be completed in March, by the decision -- sorry, the 28th of March, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour. It has been -- everything that we received consent has been disclosed. There are some items where we are still in correspondence with the provider, and we simply cannot provide, we simply cannot disclose material under Rule 70 absent the provider's consent so there are some providers who have been a bit slow in responding to our communications but I can -- as to those matters which we have received consent on, as to all those matters, the disclosure has been -- has been made. But there are some communications still pending.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Have you received consent from the Government of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I am not aware that that's even been an issue, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: The 31 documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm informed that those have been disclosed, that that has been resolved.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. And the United Nations?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe that it has, but again I'm not able to completely confirm that based on the information I have in front of me this morning. Unfortunately it appears that there are some deficiencies in the way some of the material has been described. It's very generic and just says "Rule 70 material." I cannot give a further break down of which categories it includes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It would not be proper much me to inquire about any specific international organisations but that's the remaining group. But it seemed to me there could be no excuse for Croatia or the United Nations not having attended to the matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I don't know if I can express an opinion, Your Honour, about excuse. The bottom line for the OTP is that we either have the providers' consent or not. If it's withheld, it's withheld, and under Rule 70 we simply do not have any ability to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Holding is one thing. Just failing to deal with it is another.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I agree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You can take action in respect of a failure to deal with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Absolutely, Your Honour, and that's the point. Going back to what I said a few moments ago, I know there's ongoing communications and follow-up with some of the providers saying "this is overdue," "please respond," "please let us hear from you."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, that clearly requires future attention.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Other wise has Rule 07 disclosure been completed, Mr. Scott?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, as I indicated as to those material where the provider has been consented, then that material has been provided.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Don't sit too quickly, Mr. Scott. Agreed facts?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Your Honour, there has not been progress on that point. The work on the amended indictment consumed more of our time than we had frankly expected that it would and that has consumed the majority of our time the last -- last six weeks that we were working on that prior to its filing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, as you realise, it was going to be attended to, following the last conference, within two months.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I made an observation earlier about the case drifting. I will underline it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I appreciate the Chamber's concern, and your concern, Your Honour. Having said that, frankly, it's my understanding that all sides have not had any lack of things to do, I have not received any complaints from the Defence. I think everyone has been moving forward. Yes, there are still much to do before this case can be fully ready for trial.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well. You will need, before our next conference, to have shared a proposed set of agreed facts with the Defence, hopefully in time for them to sensibly consider it --

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: -- and respond so that we know where we are. In other words, not the night before the next conference.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: Yes, understood.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Are there any other matters, Mr. Scott, that you would wish to raise?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, except I think perhaps I'd at least take the opportunity in the matters the Chamber's -- that you've raised, is that if we are able to move forward on such things as agreed facts it may at some point based on our experience and other cases may in fact require the Chamber or the Senior Legal Officer perhaps to play an active role. Quite honestly, I'm not casting any stones toward the other side of the courtroom, please make that clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You're in a rather -- glass house at the moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: I know that, Your Honour that's the reason I'm approaching it delicately but nonetheless sincerely that, given the Chamber's concerns, it doesn't do us very -- do us any good, frankly, for the Prosecution to submit proposed agreed facts that then don't go anywhere. And in most of our cases, in most of the OTP cases in the last several years, that's basically what's happened. They are sent out, there is no effective response, and simply, frankly, at the end of the day we've wasted, spent a great deal of time preparing documents that never go anywhere. I take the responsibility quite transparently for the fact that we need to take the next step. I simply take the opportunity to bring to the Chamber's attention that for that step to bear fruit, it may very well require further judicial involvement in the future based on the track record of our office that these things simply don't go anywhere. And I just take the opportunity to point that out to the Chamber. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Chamber has no observation at this point. It would be quite premature. Now, Mr. Prodanovic, is there any matter that you would wish to raise?

utterances.speaker: MR. PRODANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. We have nothing particular to raise at this point in time except in relation to what you just asked the OTP about. We are still waiting for a proposal from the OTP related to the agreed facts. As far as the Ademi case is concerned, we have very good cooperation at the pre-trial stage with the OTP and we were assisted in this by the senior legal assistant. We've managed to clarify a great deal of moot facts but that was after the indictment was confirmed. At this point in time we are facing a different situation. We are facing an amended and expanded indictment. So what the Defence is doing now, we are waiting for the final version and then we shall declare our position on it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, as I've indicated, you should have that shortly. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PRODANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Separovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPAROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. We agree on this. It's only once we've received the final version of the indictment that we can continue and work on the agreed facts. That's one thing. But I do agree with my learned friend and colleague, Mr. Scott, that first we have to deal with the objection to the indictment and only then can we go on and deal with the agreed facts. I think there is no reason for us not to continue to have a very satisfactory level of cooperation with the OTP on this matter. Thank you. And there is another thing that I'd like to raise, Your Honour. My colleague Mr. Mikulicic would like to say something about the change in the conditions of detention or rather the change in the decision on provisional release.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if I may, I would like to briefly use this opportunity and bring to your attention the poor health of our client, Mr. Markac. Ever since his provisional release he has continued to receive treatment. He has spent the last 90 days in hospital and the situation he's facing now is he has a recommendation from his doctor to spend the summer months somewhere on the sea coast. He happens to own a flat on the Croatian coast which is about 150 kilometres from Zagreb, the capital. It is because of this that the Defence will address the Chamber with a motion for redefining the terms of the provisional release of our client. I'm just using this opportunity to announce our intention and also, if I can please receive any instructions from the Chamber in case there should be any problems regarding this motion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, thank you for mentioning the matter. There is no motion yet so I am not in a position to know whether there will be any problems. So I don't know that I can assist you in any way at the present time. But if there is to be a motion based upon medical grounds, it will be dealt with on its merits when it arrives. In the meantime, I think I might ask for the name of his doctor. I think summer by the sea would be of great interest to me as well. Very well. May I thank you all for your attendance and assistance. Clearly, there has not been a satisfactory progression of this matter since the last Status Conference, and it will be necessary for there to be a significant change before we next assemble. By then, we should have the final indictment and matters can proceed in a more satisfactory way. Mr. Scott?

utterances.speaker: MR. SCOTT
utterances.text: With Your Honour's indulgence, lest there be some impression left of some inactivity on the Prosecution's part, which I think is -- would not be, with all respect, entirely fair although admittedly there are some things that need to be addressed. Since the last time that we met the Prosecution has provided approximately 479 additional documents to the Defence. I think eight video cassettes of items, and at least three transcripts, transcribed witness statements or testimony. We've also engaged in a great deal of effort with the Rule 70 providers. So, Your Honour, if the Court -- if you'll allow me, yes, we need -- there is more that needs to be done but there has been in fact considerable activity by the Prosecution since the last Status Conference, and indeed a lot of effort went into the amended indictment which hopefully will move the case forward as the Chamber rules in the near future. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well. We will adjourn now and I look forward to seeing you all in about another 120 days.
